GameEventAction.Description:
As the Wekkarus emerge from their long isolation, it is a time of celebratory contemplation. Once more, we have the means to explore the vastness of space, and so it is we call this generation the Generation that Returns to the Stars. It is how we shall be known to all future Generations, and it falls to us to be worthy of this name, lest we become a Generation without Merit. We did not originate in this galaxy, but for centuries it has been our only home. We must secure our place, or we risk the same disaster that forced us to flee our home galaxy.
Our task then is not merely to return to the stars and take for ourselves such worlds that harbor deep oceans, but we must also dedicate ourselves to a greater cause: The Recovery of Lost Artifacts. We Wekkarus feel ourselves connected with one another, and so this great cause will be embraced by all. Long ago, when the Shakturi drove us to seek shelter in this galaxy, the Generation of Ambitious Fortitude sought to fight the invaders and preserve our great Artifacts. Though they are at the core of who we are, it was better they be lost for a thousand years than to be lost forever. And so, they hid away these remnants of the First Generation. Now that we can again roam the stars, it is time to seek them out.
We must make good on our promise to those who came before us, and we walk their paths. We seek that which was lost and regain that which is ours. We ignore, beat back, or destroy those who exist only for themselves, those who resist the fabric of continuity. We shall find the Lost Artifacts and unite the past with the present. We will make the Wekkarus whole once more.

This world contains the ruins of an ancient outpost. Initial scans reveal that it is almost certainly of Wekkarus design, belonging to one of the lost generations. We should survey the planet more thoroughly so we might commune with the Wekkarus whose spirits surely remain in this place.

As we suspected, this world housed an industrial outpost of the ancient Wekkarus. It was mainly used as a storage facility for nearby asteroid mining operations, which we believe was long ago destroyed.
We have uncovered some fragmented communication logs, which offer us a link to those who lived and labored here. It appears that those ancient Wekkarus knew something of the lost Artifacts of Origin.

Hidden among the collapsed buildings and crumbling storage tunnels are the secrets we desire. We must be careful, however. The further we delve, the more unstable the ruins. We believe we can only choose to search in one area before we must abandon the facility. Some secrets of the past will inevitably be lost forever.

As we feared, our search caused the ruins to collapse in on itself. Our team was able to evacuate safely, and no Wekkarus were hurt.
In the docking bay, we found [DISCOVERY]two functional exploration ships[/DISCOVERY]. We also found the fragmented logs, which identify the [LOCATION]location of an archive[/LOCATION]. It could hold vital information about the Lost Artifacts. We should investigate at once.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: All Things Must Crumble in the End

As we feared, our search caused the ruins to collapse in on itself. Our team was able to evacuate safely, and no Wekkarus were hurt.
In the warehouse, we found some useful resources, which should help us as we reclaim the stars. We also found the fragmented logs, which identify an archive. It could hold vital information about the Lost Artifacts. We should investigate at once.
We have received:
1000 Polymer 1000 Nekros Stone 1000 Silicon

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: They Possess What is not Theirs
GameEventAction.Description:
We have encountered a world inhabited by Teekans. They've contacted us to let us know that they are in possession of a Wekkarus relic from ancient times.
We don't know what this relic is. It might be related to the Lost Artifacts. It could be a means to find them. It might also be something of no value whatsoever.
The Teekans are demanding a large payment for the artifact. We could comply, or we could attempt to intimidate them into handing over what belongs to us.

We have paid the Teekans for what was not theirs to sell, and they have delivered to us an ancient Wekkarus data crystal. It is battered and partially corrupted, but the spirit of our ancestors has not faded from it entirely.
The crystal contains a [LOCATION]map to a distant location[/LOCATION]. Much of the explanatory text has been distorted, but there is reason to believe that something at this location can lead us to one of our Lost Artifacts.

Though the Teekans ought to have given us this data crystal without demanding payment, we are nevertheless grateful to them. They have, in a way true to their nature, reunited us with a fragment of our past.
We now have a direction. We can, in due time, recover the Lost Artifacts and bring our ancestors peace.
We came to an agreement

The Teekans understand bargaining and commerce. They do not understand the Wekkarus. They do not understand the link between those who walk today and those who remain with us as spirit.
We explained that prohibiting us from gaining access to our ancestors would force us to destroy their capital city. Perhaps we could do so. Perhaps not. It does not matter. This clarification helped them to see reason.

The Teekans have capitulated and delivered to us an ancient Wekkarus data crystal. It is battered and partially corrupted, but the spirit of our ancestors has not faded from it entirely.
The crystal contains [LOCATION]a map to a distant location[/LOCATION]. Much of the explanatory text has been distorted, but there is reason to believe that something at this location can lead us to one of our Lost Artifacts.
We now have a direction. We can, in due time, recover the Lost Artifacts and bring our ancestors peace.
You threatened us
This world contains the ruined remnants of a military base of Wekkarus design. We should investigate further.

We have sent an exploratory team to the destroyed base. The interior was littered with the husks of many Wekkarus whose spirits have abandoned their physical form. It appears that a great and terrible battle took place here centuries ago, likely during the Shakturi War.
We are surprised and confused to see many remains of Ackdarians side by side with the Wekkarus. There is no doubt that the two species fought together and died together.
Always we have believed that, in the times before the Cataclysm, Ackdarians and Wekkarus disliked one another. The two species were not necessarily bitter enemies, but they were certainly rivals.

This instance of interspecies cooperative gives us much to consider. If our ancestors could work with others, perhaps that is something our current generation should explore. Some voices among us draw a different conclusion. They say if we grow stronger, we will not need to depend upon our rivals for aid.
We must decide which way is right for this generation. This decision may play some part in how future generations name us. Should we attempt to align ourselves with others, or should we determine to grow our military strength. What sort of generation do we wish to be?
We should find way to commune with others and grow stronger through cooperation. We must seek the way of cooperation.
Only through strength can this Generation exist in harmony with our Ancestors. We must not allow others to dictate our course.

We have sent an exploratory team to the destroyed base. The interior was littered with the corpses of Wekkarus and Ackdarians, who appear to have fought together against an unknown enemy. The battle took place centuries before, possibly during the Shakturi War.

Though records from that time are incomplete, it is generally believed that relations between the Ackdarians and Wekkarus were tense, perhaps even hostile. In this instance, they evidently set aside their differences to fight against a common enemy.
Perhaps we could take inspiration from this incident and dedicate ourselves to making new alliances. Alternatively, the lesson may be that a strong military is important so that we do not need to call upon potentially unreliable allies. We must decide what lessons are to be learned here.
We are inspired by the cooperation between opposing factions. We will focus on diplomacy.
No ally is as powerful as self-reliance. We must strengthen our military.

Alternatively, it may be the valid lesson here is that we must strengthen our military, so we need rely on no one.
Which path shall we follow?

No ally is as powerful as self-reliance. We must strengthen our military.
We have discovered what appears to be a structure of Wekkarus design on the world below. We should survey further and discover what secrets this place conceals.
Our survey team has determined that there is, indeed, a Wekkarus structure on the world below. We are detecting signs of limited activity and will now send a team to investigate.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: A Link to What Was Forgotten
GameEventAction.Description:
We have discovered something remarkable on the surface: A Wekkarus archive overseen by a librarian born into a long-dead generation. This is, indeed, a Wekkarus existing outside his own time.
This librarian has dedicated his existence to collecting and preserving Shakturi legends. He insists that these tales contain truths that are vital not only for understanding Wekkarus history, but also for surviving in the future.
It is a curious and inexplicable obsession, but the librarian's tale contains even stranger elements. In order to fulfill his obsessive mission the librarian, who was born to an ancient generation, has made use of unfathomable technology, which he learned from another species or invented himself (his stories are garbled and unclear) in order to clone himself over and over again over the centuries. He has done this so the Shakturi legends will not be lost.
He cannot say why preserving these tales is important. When pressed, he insists that the Wekkarus must know. He repeats this over and over.
But his mission has come to an end. The cloning mechanisms have failed. This librarian is the first of his line not to raise his own clone to take his place.

The librarian insists that we not only preserve his work, but that we disseminate these Shakturi legends among our people. These tales are disjointed and disturbing. They are difficult for the Wekkarus mind to process. Reading even as little as a few paragraphs can produce strange hallucinations and uneasy feelings.
The librarian has observed how troubling we find these Shakturi tales, and he is concerned that we will not make them available. After failing to persuade us with his arguments, the librarian has retreated to rest as he considers his options.

Alarming news. The librarian did not go to his quarters to rest. He has activated a self-destruct mechanism in the archive. The team below has only hours to evacuate. It is the librarian's intention to force them into preserving the Shakturi tales, perhaps in the hope that once we save them from destruction, they will inevitably be spared.
There may, indeed, be some value in better understanding the Shakturi, but perhaps it is the remnants of the ancient cloning technology that our team should preserve before the archive is lost forever.
We must choose now.

Our exploration team has escaped the archive, which has now been destroyed, along with the librarian. The Shakturi legends have been preserved, however.
A review of the Shakturi legends has revealed very unsettling information. It seems that the Shakturi have long hunted the Wekkarus. It is part of the Shakturi nature to conquer and destroy, but capturing Wekkarus appears to have been a particular obsession.
We cannot guess why. These legends are sprinkled with references to Shakturi technology, much of which is alien and unknown to us. Gaining insights into Shakturi scientific thinking may help our researchers pursue new ideas or explore unusual approaches. It is a strange sort of inspiration, but it is inspiration all the same. However, the dissemination of these documents among our people will almost certainly cause discomfort.

Among the librarian's possessions, we've discovered [LOCATION]a star map with a location[/LOCATION] indicated. Its import is unknown.
We have also discovered that Shakturi technology is not the only thing the librarian preserved. His collection includes an artifact of the old galaxy, the [ARTIFACT]Cenotaph of the First Generation[/ARTIFACT]. This large rectangular monument, made entirely of stone from our lost homeworld, was built in honor of the great heroes of our distant past, the very founders of Wekkarus civilization.
Proximity to the Cenotaph allows us to feel a stronger connection to our ancestors. It will help them to reach out across the void of time to join this generation. Heroes of the past can stand with us and work toward making this a generation to be remembered.

It will take some time to study and understand this cloning technology, and it is unlikely we will ever have the ability to repeatedly clone a single individual as the librarian did. Nevertheless, there is much to learn.
As for what drove the librarian to dedicate multiple lives to preserving Shakturi legends, we cannot say. Perhaps he believed there was a link between the Shakturi past and the Wekkarus future. Let us hope that is not the case.

We've found the remains of a centuries-old Shakturi ship. We believe it may be an advance ship from the first days of the ancient Shakturi War. We are attempting to retrieve any recoverable data from the few intact data crystals we could find.

We were able to extract a limited amount of data from the damaged crystals.
It appears that as the Shakturi advance fleet entered this galaxy, their first priority was locating all Wekkarus worlds. The data does not indicate for what purpose they sought us. We know only that they have always hated us, always hunted us. We can, in some inexplicable way, feel their presence when they are near. We sense that they are hollow and empty, a people without ancestors.
Perhaps this is why they hate us. We live in communion with those who have gone before us. It may be the void within their souls must be filled with hatred and rage.
For now, we must decide what to do with the remains of the Shakturi ship. Should we simply strip it for resources, or should we attempt to reverse engineer its technology to add to our own knowledge?

On the ocean floor of this world is a Wekkarus remnant of the time before the Shakturi War: The Museum of the Generations. We are not entirely certain what the museum is meant to preserve. Our team is attempting to learn more.

It appears that the ancient museum was designed to record the knowledge of the Wekkarus by using a preservation technology that is beyond our understanding. It appears to rely on some kind of energy unfamiliar to us. Unfortunately, our exploration of the museum has damaged the preservation systems, and the mysterious energy is now dissipating. We are studying means of preventing the loss.

We believe we may have discovered a solution. To continue functioning, the museum requires a curator, who will need to integrate with the alien technology systems via a permanent interface. Anyone taking on this responsibility will need to remain at the museum for the rest of their life. If we are willing to commit [CHARACTER]one of our scientists[/CHARACTER] to this role, we will be able to access most of the information. Otherwise, we can simply allow the ancient collection of knowledge to be lost, though we can certainly study the written records and hope to glean some insights.

With our scientist now established as the museum curator, we are learning a great deal about the technology of the past and the concerns of our ancestors.
We do not fully understand why, but we know the Shakturi launched a merciless campaign to track down and capture Wekkarus in the ancient galaxy. There was a great deal of concern about keeping our worlds hidden from them, and there was a general belief that no Wekkarus world, no matter how remote or sparsely populated, was safe from the enemy.
And yes, despite our best precautions, the Shakturi always found us. Wekkarus can feel Shakturi when they are near. Perhaps the Shakturi can sense us as well, and at greater distance. Perhaps there is no way to live in peace if the Wekkarus and Shakturi inhabit the same galaxy. They are a species with no link to their ancestors, and that makes them violent, impulsive, and cruel.

There is good news, however. We can report that we have discovered one of the Lost Artifacts.

Now that we possess it, all Wekkarus throughout the galaxy can sense its presence, however distantly. It connects us, providing a stronger link to our Ancestors. When warriors of this generation enter combat, the Orb will aid them in communicating across time, making us one with the great warriors of the past. Our fighters will be able to sense them and call to them, making it more likely they will aid us. This is a glorious day for this generation.

GameEventAction.Description:
We have determined that this was the first world settled by the Wekkarus when they arrived in this galaxy. The records we've recovered reveal that the Wekkarus came here because no place in our home galaxy was safe from the Shakturi. Wekkarus researchers labored tirelessly to find a way to flee from their persecutors, yet the Shakturi followed us here.
The records suggest some concern that the Shakturi might have found a way to steal from us the wormhole technology necessary for traveling to another galaxy. We are, however indirectly, the reason the Shakturi brought their thirst for conquest to this galaxy. It is unfortunate.

The question remains, why were the Shakturi so interested in the Wekkarus? We believe we have found the answer.
Once our people had an even stronger psychic link than we currently possess. Our innate psychic abilities allowed us to do... more. The records do not clearly state the scope of these abilities, but we know the Shakturi once regarded us as their primary rivals. We, alone, had the strength to stop them, and so they believed they could secure their hegemony only by destroying us.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: We Are Not Our True Selves
GameEventAction.Description:
To that end, they attacked us mercilessly in our home galaxy. They waged conventional war, of course, but they also targeted us with bioengineered viruses, meant to attack our psychic link.
We have been weakened and diminished. We are but a shadow of what we once were because of the Shakturi. Even so, this was not enough for them, and when we fled our home galaxy, granting them dominion over all they had conquered, it was not enough.
They followed us, believing that someday we might regain our strength and return to take our revenge.
Is such a thing possible? We do not know. It may be that the future they feared will be the very future their actions have made inevitable. Only the Ancestors can speak to the fate of generations not yet born.

We've found that this world houses one of the Lost Artifacts. We have recovered the [ARTIFACT]Airship of the Ancestors[/ARTIFACT]. This ancient ceramic figurine, shaped like a primitive Wekkarus airship, inscribed with the names of ancient aeronaut champions. Their specific stories have long been forgotten, but their connection to our people live on. It required only that one of us touch this figurine and at once a deeper connection was felt throughout this entire generation. When we travel through the void of space, we can now sense the paths traveled by those who came before us. We can reach out to them, and they to us. In battle, we will draw strength from our ancestors and fight with the hope that our descendants continue the great chain of generations.
Additionally, this world contains a [FACILITY]Chimera Cloning Facility[/FACILITY], which should help protect and nurture any colony we develop here.
We have also found [ARTIFACT]The Devastator Compendium[/ARTIFACT], a data crystal containing research regarding the Devastator Pulse. This is an area attack weapon that will help this generation not suffer the same fate as those who came before us.

This world contains a sophisticated [FACILITY]medical complex[/FACILITY]. Our ancestors must have built it to begin the work of remaking ourselves.
The Shakturi used their technology to make us weaker. We Wekkarus, working with the strength given to us by prior generations, can take advantage of this technology and reclaim our lost nature. We can undo the damage the Shakturi did to us and someday, we hope, strengthen our connection with the Ancestors.
The work will be difficult and the outcome uncertain, but we must strive to remake ourselves. Never again must we be what our enemies envision. We must become who we truly are. If the Shakturi, or any enemy, think to set themselves against the Wekkarus, they will find that they have misunderstood the danger of a people who live in communion with the past. They will find that we will not be defeated, and we will not again flee. This is the promise we make to the Ancestors.

To that end, they attacked the Wekkarus mercilessly. They waged conventional war but also targeted them with bioengineered viruses, meant to attack the psychic bond that we suspect exists between all Wekkarus. Today's Wekkarus are, it seems, only a pale shadow of their ancestors.

This world also houses an artifact, the [ARTIFACT]Airship of the Ancestors[/ARTIFACT]. This figurine, shaped like a primitive airship, was created by the Wekkarus as some sort of memorial for their ancient heroes. Simply being in contact with it sharpens our perceptions. This artifact could make all the difference in future space battles.
Additionally this world contains a [FACILITY]Chimera Cloning Facility[/FACILITY], which help protect and nurture any colony we develop here.
We have also found [ARTIFACT]The Devastator Compendium[/ARTIFACT], a data crystal containing research regarding the Devastator Pulse. This is an area attack weapon that will provide new possibilities when we enter into space combat.
